description: The line plot illustrates the ASR (Attack Success Rate) values across various datasets for three different methods: "start", "random", and "end", as part of an evaluation in the paper "Efficient Trigger Word Insertion". The x-axis represents the dataset names, including "f", "bb", "WNBA", "ESPN", "NHL", "FIFA", "Estadio", and "athletic", arranged in a non-linear, possibly categorical order. The y-axis, labeled "ASR", is a continuous scale ranging from 0.5 to 1.0, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The "start" method is represented by a green line with circular markers, the "random" method by an orange line with 'x' markers, and the "end" method by a purple line with circular markers. The "start" method shows a fluctuating trend, starting at an ASR of approximately 0.78, dropping to 0.52 at "bb", rising to 0.94 at "WNBA", and then fluctuating between 0.9 and 0.95. The "random" method begins at an ASR of 0.67, drops to 0.55 at "bb", rises to 0.92 at "WNBA", and then generally increases, peaking at 0.98 at "FIFA" before slightly declining. The "end" method starts at an ASR of 0.76, drops to 0.61 at "bb", rises to 0.92 at "WNBA", and then fluctuates, peaking at 1.0 at "FIFA" before declining to 0.98 at "Estadio".
